title: List comprehensions

spans.text: WHY USE THIS?
A comprehension transforms and filters data in one expression; a regular loop can be clearer when logic grows.
CORE EXPLANATION
A list comprehension builds a list from an iterable in one expression. It can transform items and apply a conditional filter.
EXAMPLE CODE
QUESTION: What will this code print? Predict first, then run it.

spans.code:
squares = [n * n for n in range(6) if n % 2 == 0]
print(squares)

spans.text: EXPECTED RESULT

LINE-BY-LINE WALKTHROUGH
`squares = [n * n for n in range(6) if n % 2 == 0]` — Binds the evaluated expression to a name; without the assignment, later lines cannot reuse that result.
`print(squares)` — Runs an expression; print displays a value and calls may have side effects—without the line, that action does not occur.
squares = [n * n for n in range(6) if n % 2 == 0]
— Binds the evaluated expression to a name; without the assignment, later lines cannot reuse that result.
print(squares)
— Runs an expression; print displays a value and calls may have side effects—without the line, that action does not occur.
REMEMBER
A list comprehension builds a list from an iterable in one expression.

spans.title: Watch out
spans.text: Mutating a collection while iterating can be surprising; build a new collection or iterate over a copy.
COMMON MISTAKES
Choose list, tuple, set, or dict based on ordering, uniqueness, and mutability needs.
